close_reason: Single-site fix in lib.rs:758: args["list"].as_array().unwrap_or(&vec![]) → args["list"].as_array().into_iter().flatten(). Same behaviour, no temporary Vec allocation. Only site of the idiom in the workspace; canonical jmap-mail-server does not have it (rg confirmed).
description:
`lib.rs:750`:

    for item in args["list"].as_array().unwrap_or(&vec![]) {

`vec![]` constructs a fresh `Vec<Value>`; `&vec![]` takes a reference to that temporary. The reference is valid because the temporary lives for the full statement (Rust temporary-lifetime extension), but the construction is wasteful and clippy::useless_vec flags exactly this shape — every call allocates an empty Vec just to satisfy the `unwrap_or` type.

Idiomatic:

    for item in args["list"].as_array().into_iter().flatten() {

`Option::into_iter()` plus `Iterator::flatten` produces zero items when the Option is None and the inner Vec's iterator items when Some — without ever materialising a Vec for the empty case. Same observable behaviour, no allocation, reads as 'iterate the array if present'.

Alternative: `args["list"].as_array().map(Vec::as_slice).unwrap_or(&[]).iter()` — also avoids the temporary but is wordier.

Scope: one site in test code (lib.rs:750 in `utcstart_not_in_default_properties`). Not present in canonical jmap-mail-server (`rg 'unwrap_or\(&vec!' crate-jmap-` returns this one site only). Low priority but the only site of this idiom in the workspace — fixing it prevents the pattern from spreading via copy-paste.
title: `unwrap_or(&vec![])` takes a reference to a freshly-created Vec in test loop
